note: Pilot tracker: only projects that change connectivity for a pilot industrial node. The differentiator is the 'strategic_significance' line — project → industrial consequence — which is Techadyant analysis.

projects.name: Ahmedabad–Dholera Greenfield Expressway (NE-8)
projects.implementing_agency: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways / NHAI
projects.status_note: Opened to the public for testing; final operational readiness being assessed (27 Feb 2026).
projects.strategic_significance: Turns Dholera from a two-hour drive into a ~45-minute extension of Ahmedabad and puts an expressway interchange at the airport gate — the first connectivity piece that makes the fab’s workforce, construction and air-cargo logistics practical before rail arrives.

facts.label: Travel time
facts.value: Ahmedabad–Dholera: 100 km / 2 h 15 min → 83 km / 45 min

projects.name: Ahmedabad (Sarkhej)–Dholera semi high-speed double line
projects.strategic_significance: Closes Dholera’s multimodal gap, but only from 2030-31 — after the fab’s production target. Until then, chemicals, gases and equipment move by road; that timing gap is what the node’s near-term logistics market prices in.

facts.label: Network addition
facts.value: About 134 km

facts.label: Connects
facts.value: Ahmedabad, Dholera SIR, Dholera Airport and the Lothal National Maritime Heritage Complex

projects.name: Dholera International Airport
projects.cost_note: Total cost not recorded from a primary source.
projects.status_note: ~80% complete; operations targeted Sep–Oct 2026 per the Civil Aviation Minister as reported (single trade-press source; unconfirmed).
projects.strategic_significance: For a fab, air cargo is the critical mode: spares, specialty materials and finished wafers are high-value and time-sensitive. An operational cargo hub at the SIR would cut the ~105 km straight-line dependence on Ahmedabad.

facts.label: Planned facilities
facts.value: 25,000 sq m passenger terminal; 2,500 sq m cargo hub

projects.name: Western DFC final sections (New Sanand N–New Makarpura; New Umbergaon–New Saphale; New Saphale–New JNPT)
projects.cost_note: Aggregate for the three sections (326 route km), 'more than ₹20,700 crore'
projects.status_note: Dedicated 8 Sep 2026; WDFC completed and fully operational.
projects.strategic_significance: Puts a dedicated freight-rail station inside India’s first operating chip-packaging cluster and completes the Dadri–JNPA spine that also serves the Jewar side. Rail does not carry chips — it carries the gases, chemicals, packaging materials and containerised output that make a cluster cheaper to run.

facts.label: Route km dedicated
facts.value: 326 km across three sections

facts.label: Full corridor
facts.value: WDFC 1,506 km Dadri–JNPT completed and fully operational

projects.name: Noida International Airport, Jewar — Phase 1
projects.project_type: Greenfield international airport with integrated cargo terminal
projects.cost_note: Approximate total investment for Phase 1 per AIR
projects.status_note: Phase 1 inaugurated 28 Mar 2026; first cargo flight 17 Jun 2026.
projects.strategic_significance: Gives the India Chip OSAT an operating cargo airport next door before the plant ships its first unit — inverting the usual Indian sequence in which factories wait years for logistics.

facts.label: Phase 1 capacity
facts.value: 12 million passengers/yr; > 2.5 lakh t cargo/yr (expandable to ~18 lakh t)

projects.name: Road over bridge at LC-235, Deendayal Port (Kandla)
projects.project_type: Port-connectivity road over bridge at a rail level crossing
projects.status_note: Approved by MoPSW after appraisal by its Delegated Investment Board (reported 4 Apr 2026).
projects.strategic_significance: A small project with a specific aim: removing a rail–road conflict point at a major port gate. Sagarmala’s port-connectivity pillar works at this level of grain, and a port’s effective capacity depends on it as much as on berths.

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: ₹132.51 crore (Sagarmala-funded)

projects.name: Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway (greenfield)
projects.cost_note: Rs 17,900 crore estimate (India Infra Hub, Feb 2020); current sanctioned package costs not captured.
projects.status_note: Described as being developed under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I (Jun 2026); construction progress and opening date not stated. Alignment begins at Hoskote (Karnataka) and ends at Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu), with last-mile to Chennai via two elevated connectors.
projects.strategic_significance: Bharatmala’s economic-corridor logic, visible on the ground: an expressway named as a priority corridor of an industrial corridor, with industrial areas and a proposed MMLP along its Karnataka section.

projects.name: Delhi–Mumbai Expressway (Delhi–Vadodara–Mumbai Greenfield Expressway)
projects.cost_note: Approximately Rs 1 lakh crore per PIB (Jun 2026); Rs 1.10 lakh crore reported Jul 2026.
projects.status_note: ~80% complete per the Road Transport Minister (Jul 2026), with full completion signalled within two years. Sections opened progressively since Feb 2023.
projects.corridor: Delhi–Mumbai freight axis (Bharatmala flagship; road-side complement to the Western DFC)
projects.strategic_significance: India’s longest access-controlled expressway compresses the Delhi–Mumbai trunk onto a 1,386 km 8-lane corridor with a dedicated JNPT spur — the road-side complement to the Western DFC that will shape where North–South warehousing and distribution capacity consolidates.

projects.name: Delhi–Amritsar–Katra Expressway
projects.cost_note: Estimated around Rs 38,905 crore (NDTV, Jul 2026); commonly cited planning figure ~Rs 40,000 crore.
projects.status_note: First 157.92 km (Packages 1–5, ~Rs 9,680 crore) dedicated to the nation on 17 Jul 2026; balance under construction.
projects.strategic_significance: Gives the Punjab agro-industrial belt and the Jammu–Katra pilgrimage economy a high-speed access-controlled spine toward NCR; its Katra leg doubles as border-region connectivity. The Bharatmala classification rests on secondary sources — upgrade when a sanction document is captured.

facts.label: First stretch

projects.name: Amritsar–Jamnagar Expressway (Economic Corridor EC-3)
projects.cost_note: Total corridor cost not captured from a primary source. The dedicated Rajasthan section alone was built at around Rs 11,125 crore (PIB, Jul 2023).

projects.name: Zojila Tunnel (NH-1 Srinagar–Leh)
projects.cost_note: Total project cost Rs 6,809.69 crore (PIB, Aug 2024).
projects.status_note: Final breakthrough achieved 9 Jun 2026; opening targeted around February 2028 (reported).
projects.strategic_significance: The programme’s border-connectivity face: converting a seasonally blocked Himalayan pass into an all-weather Srinagar–Leh freight and personnel axis for Ladakh — strategic access first, with civilian logistics and tourism as second-order effects.
